classifiedFindings.label: M-01
classifiedFindings.title: A broadcast run performs ZERO on-chain verification of its own outcome: Phase 7 executes in forge's local pass, and the compensating human check is unticked

classification.assetImpact: No assets are stolen, lost or made unrecoverable. The impact is on PROTOCOL FUNCTION AND AVAILABILITY: a half-applied cutover leaves one or more of the five dispatcher indices in the fail-closed intermediate state the story itself documents (`hook.setDispatcher(new)` landed, `replaceDispatcher(idx, new)` not), so mints on that index revert `OnlyDispatcher` indefinitely rather than intermittently, and nothing in the tooling raises a signal. Secondary: donor->streamer routing, batch-minter whitelist/stream registration and staker migration can each be left one-sided.
attackPath: 1. No attacker is required. The precondition is ordinary broadcast-time divergence: an on-chain revert, a state drift between the local pass and dispatch, or an operator abort mid-session.
2. `run()` executes the entire Solidity body ONCE in forge's local pass, collecting calldata; ~60 transactions are then signed on the Ledger and dispatched afterwards.

3. Every safety assertion in the script - Phase 0 preconditions, in-phase post-conditions (BPT conservation :892-895, newBM balance unchanged :728-731, `old.paused()` :1134, `V1 totalStaked == 0` :1394) and the whole of Phase 7 - has therefore ALREADY evaluated, against local pre-broadcast state, before transaction #1 leaves the machine. They assert that the PLAN is internally consistent, never that the CHAIN matches it.
4. Phase 8 (which contains the BLOCKING probes) does not execute under `--broadcast` at all.
5. The story's designated compensating control is checklist line 1195, a '(Post-broadcast, HUMAN step)' item. It is UNTICKED.
6. Net: on the broadcast path there is no outcome verification of any kind. The system can be left half-configured over live funds with no automated and no procedural detection.
classification.likelihood: medium - no adversary and no special conditions; requires only that something diverges during a multi-hour, 60+-transaction Ledger session over live mainnet state. The fork dry run is evidence the HAPPY path is sound; it is not evidence about the divergent path, because the fork run was PREVIEW and Phase 7 there ran against a state the same process had just produced locally.
classification.assumptions: That at least one transaction in the broadcast sequence lands differently from, or fails relative to, the locally-simulated plan. Stated, not hidden.
classification.externalRequirements: Mainnet state drift or a transaction failure during the session; an operator who does not independently perform the unticked line-1195 on-chain confirmation.
classification.recoverability: Recoverable by owner action (all mutation targets remain owner-controlled and `migrate` / `:resume` are re-runnable) - but recovery is gated on someone NOTICING, which is precisely what this finding says is absent.

severityDebate.whyNotHigh: C4 High requires assets stolen/lost/compromised directly or via a valid attack path with no hand-wavy hypotheticals. There is no attacker, no theft path, and no demonstrated route to unrecoverable loss - every affected contract stays owner-controlled and the fork run showed zero unintended state writes. Escalating an assurance-and-availability defect to High would be exactly the overstatement that dilutes a report.
severityDebate.whyMediumAndNotLow: Three facts jointly clear the Medium bar and none of them is hypothetical: (a) the undetected end state is a real availability impact - mint indices reverting `OnlyDispatcher` past the intended fail-closed window - not merely 'we would not have a report'; (b) the compensating control is not merely weak, it is ABSENT on the broadcast path, because the only outcome check the design defines (line 1195) is unticked at the time of this audit; (c) this defect is the ENABLING condition that converts three other Lows in this set from theoretical to undetectable - PR-11's stated backstop `require(old.totalStaked() == 0)` at :1394, PR-02's trailing `require(balanceOf(OLD_BATCH_MINTER) == 0)` at :1148, and PR-06's BPT conservation all evaluate in the same local pass. That is 'protocol function or availability could be impacted, with stated assumptions and external requirements' - the C4 Medium shape.

limbRejected.limb: 'a 60+-tx one-shot cutover can exit 0 while half-applied' / 'forge exiting 0 while a tx reverted on-chain'
limbRejected.ruling: EXCLUDED FROM THE SEVERITY BASIS. The fork run was PREVIEW, so forge's `--broadcast --skip-simulation --slow` receipt-handling and exit-code behaviour on a reverted on-chain transaction was NOT observed in this audit; it is reasoned, not evidenced. Under Law 1 the finding is not dropped, but an unverified limb must not carry a severity. The Medium therefore rests ONLY on the verified structural facts: Phase 7 and every in-phase assertion evaluate before dispatch (read directly from run():400-411 and the local-pass execution model), Phase 8 is gated off under broadcast (run():402-408), and line 1195 is unticked (read verbatim from the story). Those three hold regardless of what forge's exit code does.
limbRejected.actionForReport: State the exit-code question as an OPEN OPERATIONAL QUESTION for the operator to confirm before the session, not as a finding claim.

severityDebate.oneShotWeight: Applied. On a redeployable contract, 'no post-deployment verification entry point' would be routine hardening. Here the operation cannot be re-run cleanly, the operator gets one Ledger session, and the designated human backstop is unticked - which is what moves it over the line rather than merely up the Low ordering.

classifiedFindings.label: L-01
classifiedFindings.title: A user who stakes between snapshot generation and the on-chain pause is silently stranded on a paused, defunded, Pauser-deregistered V1 staker

classification.assetImpact: An end user's staked NFT position and its future emissions become UNAVAILABLE on a retired contract. No value is destroyed and nothing is transferred to a third party: the position remains on V1, the owner retains `setPauser`/`unpause`, `migrate` is re-runnable by design, and V1 can be re-funded or V2 topped up.
attackPath: 1. No attacker. `snapshot-depletion-stakers.js` freezes the user list at block N; forge's local pass freezes it a second time.

2. `NFTStakerDepletion.stake` is UNGATED during `Migrating` (NFTStakerDepletion.sol:550, audit-20 M-05), and V1 is not actually paused until the `st_<label>_pause` transaction lands on-chain - potentially hours into the Ledger session.
3. A user stakes inside that window. Their address is absent from `users`, so `migrate(users)` skips them.

4. The stated backstop `require(old.totalStaked() == 0, "V1 still holds stake after migrate - widen the snapshot and re-run")` at :1394 cannot catch it: like all of Phase 6 it evaluates in the local pass against pre-broadcast state (see M-01).
5. Step 9 then sweeps V1's reward budget down to a ~1% residual, and V1 has already been unregistered from the global `Pauser`, so a later `Pauser.unpause()` will not reach it.
6. The user is left staked on a paused, defunded, unreachable-by-global-unpause contract, with no automatic detection.
classification.likelihood: low - requires a real user to stake inside the snapshot-to-pause window. The population is 6 stakers across the three contracts (2 / 146 / 13 units). Probability is a direct function of snapshot staleness, and the story's 'Open items carried to review' already instructs re-running the snapshot immediately before the session.
classification.assumptions: A user stakes during the window; the operator does not re-run the snapshot immediately before the session.
classification.externalRequirements: Live user activity concurrent with the multi-hour Ledger session.
classification.recoverability: Full, by owner action - but manual and undetected until someone looks.

severityDebate.whyHeldAtLow: This was the closest call in the set - it is the only candidate with a concrete end-user harm narrative, and its designed backstop is vacuous on the very path that matters. It is held at Low for one decisive reason the other near-Medium candidates lack: a DESIGNATED, SUFFICIENT DETECTION CONTROL EXISTS AND IS SPECIFIC TO THIS FAILURE. Story checklist line 1195 requires the operator to confirm on-chain that 'each V1 staker has `totalStaked == 0`' - which is exactly the condition that catches a skipped user, read from the chain rather than from the local pass. Unlike M-01, whose whole subject is the absence of that control, PR-11's failure mode is inside its coverage. Combined with full recoverability, an owner who retains every lever, a 6-address population, and an operator instruction already recorded in the story, the honest classification is Low.
severityDebate.whyNotDownToQA: Because the harm is real user asset UNAVAILABILITY, not a state-handling nicety, and because the guard the authors wrote to prevent it does not function on the broadcast path. That is a genuine Low, not informational.
severityDebate.oneShotWeight: Applied as ORDERING: L-01, the top Low in the set.
severityDebate.conditionalMediumReopenTrigger: RE-CLASSIFY AS MEDIUM if ANY of the following holds at broadcast time: (a) story-072 checklist line 1195 is still unticked when the Ledger session begins - the sole reason this is Low is that a specific, sufficient detection control is designated, and an unticked control is not a control; (b) the snapshot is older than a documented freshness bound at consumption time; (c) the staker population grows materially beyond the 6 addresses observed at block 25659373. This trigger must be carried into the ledger entry verbatim.

classifiedFindings.recommendation:
Close the window rather than narrow it: split the pause out of the frozen plan. Either (a) pause all three V1 stakers in a separate, short broadcast BEFORE generating the snapshot, so the user list is taken against an already-frozen contract - the snapshot header's 'does NOT need to be taken after a pause' rationale then no longer applies and the list becomes provably final; or (b) add a hard freshness gate: record the snapshot's `blockNumber` in the JSON (it already is) and `require(snapshotBlock >= block.number - N)` in Phase 0 so a stale list cannot be consumed at all. (b) is cheap and also fixes PR-03's late-failure problem. Independently, keep the story's 'Open items carried to review' instruction - re-run `promotion-ready:snapshot` immediately before the session - as an operator gate.

CLASSIFIER ADDENDUM: option (a) is the only one that CLOSES the window; (b) only narrows it. If (b) is chosen, the conditional-Medium reopen trigger above stays armed.
classifiedFindings.recommendationQuality: strong - two concrete options with the difference between closing and narrowing stated explicitly

remediationOverlapPreserved.note: A Phase 0 `require(snapshotBlock >= block.number - N)` would narrow PR-11's window and satisfy part of PR-03. If the owner implements PR-03's recommendation in full, re-check PR-11 for partial closure - but do not auto-close it: narrowing a window is not closing it, and the ungated NFTStakerDepletion.stake during Migrating (audit-20 M-05) is unchanged.

classifiedFindings.vacuousGuardNotePreserved: PR-11's stated backstop `require(old.totalStaked() == 0)` at :1394 is itself a member of the ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast family (it evaluates in the local pass). This is a CITATION of PR-09, not an overlap: PR-11 remains a finding even if the guard were made real, because the user would then merely halt the cutover rather than be silently skipped.
classifiedFindings.justification: Low under C4: user-facing availability of a staked position is impacted, but assets are not at risk, recovery is complete and owner-controlled, likelihood is low against a 6-address population, and a designated on-chain detection control specific to this failure exists in the story's post-broadcast checklist. Escalating to Medium would require that control to be absent - which is exactly the reopen trigger recorded above.

classifiedFindings.label: L-02
classifiedFindings.title: Phase 7's BPT conservation assertion degrades to `>= 0` on every resume path, leaving the largest asset in the cutover unverified exactly when verification matters most

classification.assetImpact: None demonstrated. 16,338.8190 BPT is the largest single asset in the closure and the assertion intended to confirm its arrival becomes `balanceOf(newPooler) >= 0` on any resume leg where the move already landed. But the audit could not construct a state in which the BPT actually goes astray: the six `_moveBPT` guard rails were independently assessed as effective in EVERY enumerated resume branch. The loss is one layer of defence-in-depth, not custody.
attackPath: 1. No attacker. A first broadcast leg completes the BPT move (`OLD_POOLER` -> `newPooler`) and the session is then interrupted.
2. The operator runs `:resume`. Phase 0 re-reads `bptAtPhase0 = IERC20(BALANCER_POOL).balanceOf(OLD_POOLER)` at :505; the old pooler is now empty, so `bptAtPhase0 == 0`.

3. Phase 7's `require(IERC20(BALANCER_POOL).balanceOf(newPooler) >= bptAtPhase0)` therefore reduces to `>= 0` - unconditionally true, and would remain true even if the 16,338 BPT sat on a third address.
4. The companion `require(balanceOf(OLD_POOLER) == 0)` at :1563 still holds, but 'the old pooler is empty' and 'the new pooler is full' are different claims; only the vacuous one covers the second.
5. This is the exact step the `//promotion-ready:resume` annotation singles out as 'THE ONE STEP A BAD RESUME COULD RUIN'.
classification.likelihood: low as a detection loss (any interrupted session followed by `:resume` triggers it); effectively nil as a value-loss path, because no enumerated branch reaches a wrong-custody state that this assertion would have been the only thing to catch.
classification.assumptions: The session is interrupted after the BPT move lands and is continued via `:resume`.
classification.externalRequirements: A resume leg - i.e. a partial first session.
classification.recoverability: N/A - no loss state was demonstrated. The destination is required to expose `withdrawBPT` + `rescueERC20` and to be `owner() == OWNER`, so even a mis-sent BPT would be recoverable.

severityDebate.whyHeldAtLow: Re-examined specifically because it sits on the single largest value at risk and on the code path the runbook itself flags as highest-risk. It is held at Low because the auditor's own enumeration - which this pass accepts - closes every branch by which the BPT could actually go wrong: a phantom pooler address fails `owner() == OWNER` and `code.length > 0`; an already-zero old balance ABORTS rather than re-running; an incorrectly-trimmed `pooler_bpt` progress flag is caught by the NON-vacuous `balanceOf(OLD_POOLER) == 0`. A redundant layer becoming vacuous is a defence-in-depth regression, and C4 Medium requires an actual function/availability impact or a value leak with stated assumptions. Classifying 'the belt is decorative while the braces hold' as Medium because the asset is large would be severity-by-headline-number, which is precisely the overstatement to avoid. The size of the asset raises the ORDER, not the tier.
severityDebate.oneShotWeight: Applied as ORDERING: L-02, ranked above every other Low except the one with concrete user harm.
severityDebate.conditionalMediumReopenTrigger: RE-CLASSIFY AS MEDIUM if any of the six `_moveBPT` guard rails is weakened, removed, or refactored - they are the sole reason this is Low. In particular, M-01's recommended fix (relocating Phase 7 to a standalone post-broadcast verifier) ACTIVELY WORSENS this finding: the relocated Phase 7 would re-read `bptAtPhase0` from an already-emptied `OLD_POOLER`, making the assertion vacuous on the FRESH path too. If M-01's fix is implemented without persisting `bptAtCutover`, this becomes a Medium.
severityDebate.fixOrderingConstraint: IMPLEMENT L-02 BEFORE M-01. This is the decisive inversion the deduplicator preserved and it must survive into the report: a consolidation of L-02 into M-01, or an M-01 fix shipped alone, would silently widen this bug while reading as a resolution.

classifiedFindings.recommendation:
Persist the Phase 0 BPT reading across resumes rather than re-deriving it. Record it in the progress file as a first-class entry (the `ContractDeployment` struct already carries unused `uint256` fields, or add a sibling `bptAtCutover` key) and, when a progress file is present, assert `balanceOf(newPooler) >= recordedBpt` instead of the freshly-read zero. A cheaper stopgap: when `_isConfigured("pooler_bpt")` is true, assert `balanceOf(newPooler) > 0` at minimum, so the resume path is never fully vacuous.

CLASSIFIER ADDENDUM: land this BEFORE M-01's verification entry point, and have that entry point consume the persisted `bptAtCutover` rather than a freshly-read Phase 0 value.
classifiedFindings.recommendationQuality: strong - a primary fix plus a cheaper stopgap, both concrete

classifiedFindings.label: L-03
classifiedFindings.title: The progress file is stamped `deploymentStatus: "completed"` during the local pass, making the patch script's own gate structurally inert

classification.assetImpact: None on-chain. The blast radius is an OFF-CHAIN artefact: `mainnet-addresses.ts` patched with addresses for contracts that may never have been deployed, which then feeds the UI and downstream scripts.
attackPath: 1. No attacker. `_writeProgressFileWithStatus("completed")` is called at the end of `run()` - the end of forge's LOCAL pass, before any transaction is broadcast.
2. `_trackDeployment`/`_trackConfig` write `"in_progress"` during the same pass, so `"in_progress"` is only ever observable after a LOCAL-pass revert (which also yields a non-zero forge exit).
3. Any run that reaches the broadcast stage at all has therefore already written `"completed"` with every step marked done.

classification.likelihood: low - the two real interlocks (the `&&` short-circuit and the mandatory hand-trim) are correctly implemented and documented, and `backup-mainnet-addresses.js` runs first in the chain. The plausible trigger is a manual recovery action after a crashed broadcast, which is exactly the moment an operator improvises.

classification.externalRequirements: A crashed or partial broadcast, plus manual out-of-chain invocation.
classification.recoverability: Full - `backup-mainnet-addresses.js` precedes the patch in the chain, and the address file is version-controlled.

severityDebate.whyHeldAtLow: Re-examined specifically on the grounds that 'the resume path's provenance check carries zero information' on an irreversible operation. attackPath: 1. No attacker. `bm_.setNudgeTokenWhitelist(KENDU, true)` at :640-644 is unconditional on the broadcast path.

3. A `--broadcast` run therefore whitelists the token with the blocking gate never executing; enforcement rests entirely on the operator having run `promotion-ready:dry` first.

classification.likelihood: very low today (nil for Kendu, which is proven untaxed and immutable); latent for any future token admission.
classification.assumptions: A future third reward token is admitted on a broadcast run without a dry run first.
classification.externalRequirements: Admission of a taxed or reverting token; the M-01 no-try/catch loop remaining unfixed for the full-blast-radius variant.
classification.recoverability: Immediate - `setNudgeTokenWhitelist(token, false)` is owner-only and takes effect at once. This is availability-with-a-lever, not loss.

severityDebate.whyHeldAtLow: The availability impact is real in shape but unarmed in fact, and the remedy is a single owner transaction available at any time. It needs no cheatcode when broadcasting - the owner can fund the probe from its own Kendu balance with a small amount, or the check can be reduced to a broadcast-safe static assertion (`buyTotalFees() == 0 && sellTotalFees() == 0 && owner() == address(0)`) that the script `require`s unconditionally. classifiedFindings.label: L-05
classifiedFindings.title: Phase 4d's post-pause residue sweep can never fire, so its stated rationale and the story's 'rescueERC20 still works while paused' assertion are both unproven

classification.assetImpact: A small, bounded amount of USDC - donations landing on the old sink between Phase 3's rescue and each donor's repoint - is left on a paused, retired contract instead of entering the stream. It is NOT lost: `rescueERC20` is `onlyOwner` and is not pause-gated, so the funds are recoverable at any later time. Stranded-value-pending-a-manual-step. Explicitly NOT framed as an economic value leak.
attackPath: 1. No attacker. Autonomous Decision 2 reasons: 'Donors keep pushing USDC at the old sink for the whole interval between Phase 3's rescue and their own repoint… On the dry run the residue was 0 (Phase 3 ran seconds earlier); on a real multi-hour Ledger session it will not be.'

2. That reasoning does not survive forge's execution model. `uint256 residue = IERC20(USDC).balanceOf(OLD_BATCH_MINTER)` at :1140 is evaluated in the LOCAL pass, seconds after Phase 3's LOCAL rescue - so `residue` is 0 there too.
3. The `if (residue > 0)` branch is therefore never taken and NO rescue transaction is ever queued into the broadcast plan.
4. Whatever USDC actually accumulates on the old minter during the multi-hour broadcast is not swept.
5. The trailing `require(balanceOf(OLD_BATCH_MINTER) == 0)` at :1148 likewise evaluates only locally and passes vacuously.
6. Fork-confirmed: the run logged 'no residue to sweep'.
classification.likelihood: high that the branch never fires (it is structural, not probabilistic); low-to-moderate that a material residue accumulates, bounded by donor cadence over the session window.
classification.assumptions: Donors continue pushing USDC at the old sink during the session - which is Autonomous Decision 2's own stated premise.
classification.externalRequirements: Donor activity during the broadcast window.
classification.recoverability: Full and permanent - `rescueERC20` is `onlyOwner` and not pause-gated.

A ticked acceptance criterion claims an assertion the code only prints as a sentence.

faithfulnessDeviation.secondDeviation: Autonomous Decision 2 asserts a leak is structurally closed when it is not. That is a documented design decision contradicted by the code it describes, which is a Law-2 deviation independent of the checklist tick.

Two independent fixes. (1) Make the sweep unconditional so a rescue transaction is always queued: replace the `if (residue > 0)` branch with an unconditional `rescueERC20(USDC, OWNER, type(uint256).max)`-style full-balance call if the legacy minter supports it, or - since it does not - add an explicit post-broadcast operator step to the runbook and drop Autonomous Decision 2's claim that the leak is structurally closed. (2) Prove the pause-transparency property in Phase 8 instead: `deal` 1 USDC onto the paused old minter and assert `rescueERC20` succeeds, which is a real test rather than a comment.

CLASSIFIER ADDENDUM (limb (1) is self-negating as written and needs a decision, see recommendationQuality): the concrete form of the fallback is - add to the runbook, as a numbered post-broadcast step alongside story checklist line 1195, 'read `IERC20(USDC).balanceOf(OLD_BATCH_MINTER)`; if non-zero, call `rescueERC20(USDC, OWNER, bal)` then `forceApprove` + `collectNudge(newBM, USDC, bal)` so it enters the stream rather than the pot' - i.e. mirror Phase 3's own sequence by hand. Alternatively, if the legacy minter's `rescueERC20` accepts an explicit amount, queue a SECOND rescue unconditionally with a `try`-wrapped call so a zero-balance case is a no-op rather than a revert. Either way, Autonomous Decision 2's 'structurally closed' claim must be retracted - that part is not optional.

A finding whose primary fix retracts itself is incomplete. Not invented over: the classifier addendum above spells out the runbook step concretely and offers a try-wrapped unconditional alternative, but the OWNER must choose between them. classifiedFindings.justification: Low under C4: no assets at risk (the residue is fully recoverable via an onlyOwner, non-pause-gated `rescueERC20`), and no protocol function or availability is impacted - the old minter is being retired regardless. classification.assetImpact: Latent, none realised. Under-enumeration would strand a user's staked position on V1 - the same end state as L-01, reached by an orthogonal route. Recoverable by owner action.

classifiedFindings.label: Q-01
classifiedFindings.title: The knowingly-accepted mint-UI breakage has no tracked remediation story, so the cutover ships an indefinite outage

classification.assetImpact: None. Contracts are correct; direct and multicall callers are unaffected. User-facing mint availability via the UI is lost from the moment of broadcast until an unscheduled follow-up ships.
attackPath: 1. No attacker and no defect. Whitelisting three reward tokens makes `batchMint`'s `minRewards` array length-3, and `getNudgeTokens()` reorders on removal (swap-and-pop), so callers must re-fetch immediately before every call.
2. The `//promotion-ready` annotation and the script both record that 'the live mint UI is BROKEN until a phlimbo-ui story ships a 3-element array plus a getNudgeTokens() re-fetch'.
3. Story line 1447 states: 'The `phlimbo-ui` follow-up story … is **still unraised**. The live mint UI breaks the moment this broadcasts. Tracked as a comment at `story-dependencies.md:218`.'
4. A comment in a dependencies file is not a raised story, so the outage is unbounded in duration rather than sequenced.
classification.likelihood: certain - the breakage is deterministic on broadcast. It is also intended.
classification.recoverability: By shipping the follow-up story, whenever that is.

severityDebate.law3Analysis: The outage itself is a KNOWING, documented, priced owner decision with an OBVIOUS consequence - the owner would not be surprised - so under Law 3 it is trusted and is NOT reported as a footgun or a misconfiguration. Applying the surprise test cleanly separates two things the finding bundles: the DECISION (obvious, trusted, out of scope) and the TRACKING (a same-day-or-never outage recorded only inside a package.json comment and a comment at story-dependencies.md:218, which is the thing that can silently persist). Only the second is reportable, and it is disclosure/scheduling hygiene with no code defect - QA. This lands consistently with its class sibling, ledger Q-04 (a807cc7a), which is already `qa` and covers the complementary script-side half of the same cutover break.
severityDebate.notSuppressed: Explicitly NOT closed under the 'reckless admin mistakes' known-invalid rule. Nobody is acting recklessly and nothing is being second-guessed; the item exists to bound the duration and to move the record out of a package.json comment. The sanitizer's candour note - that a reasonable triager could legitimately close this on Law 3 - is preserved so the human decides deliberately rather than inheriting the decision from a filter.

classifiedFindings.label: Q-02
classifiedFindings.title: The Phase 6 budget top-up approval lacks the before/after allowance assertions that guard every other approval in the script

classification.assetImpact: None demonstrated. The theoretical residual is a leftover phUSD allowance from the OWNER EOA to a V2 staker - BOUNDED at `movable`, not infinite - if `topUp` ever pulled less than approved.
attackPath: 1. No attacker. `IERC20(PHUSD).approve(v2, movable); NFTStakerDepletionV2(v2).topUp(movable);` at :1409-1410 has no pre-check that the existing allowance is zero and no post-check that it returned to zero.

2. The script's own USDC donation helper `_collectNudgeFromOwner` does both and states why: 'The allowance is fully consumed inside `collectNudge`, so it always returns to 0 - asserted here so a stale approval can never silently accumulate' (:742-744, :753).
3. Three separate `approve` calls run across the three stakers with no such guard.

4. For value to move, `topUp` would have to under-pull AND the spender would have to later draw the residue - but `topUp` is `onlyOwner` on a contract deployed moments earlier in the same script, and the fork run showed exact consumption (swept 4.6326 / 708.8243 / 51.9974 phUSD with V2 balances matching).
classification.likelihood: nil on current code - there is no state in which value moves.
classification.assumptions: A `topUp` implementation that under-pulls, which the deployed source does not exhibit.

severityDebate.why: The finding's own impact statement concludes 'This is defence-in-depth parity, not a live bug', and the classification agrees: the approval is bounded, the spender is a first-party contract deployed in the same transaction sequence, `topUp` is `onlyOwner`, and the fork run showed exact consumption on all three legs. C4 QA is 'state handling, function incorrect as to spec, issues with comments'; a consistency break against the file's own documented convention with no impact path is exactly that. Calling it Low would overstate.
severityDebate.notSuppressed: The tool-noise / style carve-out remains REJECTED as a suppression basis. The defect is an asymmetry against a convention the same file establishes and documents 660 lines earlier, which no automated tool can surface. Downgrading the tier is not the same as accepting the carve-out, and the argument that defeated it is preserved verbatim in the QA report.

classifiedFindings.recommendation: Mirror the USDC helper exactly: `require(IERC20(PHUSD).allowance(OWNER, v2) == 0, "stale V2 topUp allowance");` before, `forceApprove` (or `approve`) in the middle, and `require(IERC20(PHUSD).allowance(OWNER, v2) == 0, "topUp left allowance behind");` after. Three lines per staker, and it makes the script's approval hygiene uniform - which is the actual value, since a reader currently cannot tell whether the asymmetry is deliberate.
classifiedFindings.recommendationQuality: strong - supplies the literal lines and names the real benefit (readability of intent)
classifiedFindings.justification: QA under C4: no assets at risk, no function or availability impact, and no reachable state in which value moves. It is a state-handling/consistency defect against the script's own documented standard, correctly bundled in the QA report. Downgraded from the auditor's Low because the finding's own impact analysis establishes there is no live bug.

classifiedFindings.label: Q-03
classifiedFindings.title: The new StableYieldAccumulator is given an unbounded phlimbo approval that is hardcoded rather than mirrored from the retiring instance

classification.assetImpact: None. PhlimboV2 is a first-party contract and an infinite approval to it is the conventional pattern for a pull-based reward collector.
attackPath: 1. No attacker. Phase 5 mirrors the retiring accumulator's configuration field by field - `rewardToken`, `phlimbo`, `nftMinter`, `discountRate`, three `tokenConfigs`, three strategies, `nudgeSplit` - each read live off `OLD_SYA`.
2. One value is not mirrored: `sya.approvePhlimbo(type(uint256).max)` is a hardcoded infinite approval.
3. The inline comment justifies the mechanism ('collectReward pulls via transferFrom') but not the magnitude.
4. The project's own CLAUDE.md Configuration Safety section names caps and unbounded allowances as parameters requiring explicit justification rather than a default.
classification.likelihood: nil - no impact path exists on current code.
classification.externalRequirements: A future repoint of the phlimbo dependency would be required for the unbounded magnitude to matter.

severityDebate.why: Agrees with the proposed bucket; this pass simply makes the severity field consistent with it. Weakest candidate in the set. Retained rather than dropped because it is anchored to a WRITTEN in-repo standard (project CLAUDE.md Configuration Safety) rather than auditor preference, the fix is one sentence, and Phase 5 mirrors ELEVEN values off the live retiring instance while hardcoding exactly this one. Cached known-issue #10 ('admin trust assumptions…') was considered and rejected as authority - it has no suppression standing in this project (the declared known-issues file does not exist) and would fail on the merits anyway, since a discipline break against the repo's own written standard is not an admin-trust concession.
severityDebate.recallNote: Under Law 1, keep. A QA line item costs the report almost nothing, and dropping it would remove the only record that the discipline break was noticed.

classifiedFindings.recommendation: Either read the retiring instance's existing phlimbo allowance and mirror it, or keep `type(uint256).max` and extend the comment to record why unbounded is correct here (PhlimboV2 is first-party, the approval is scoped to one spender, and `collectReward` is the only consumer) so the choice reads as deliberate rather than defaulted.
